p: a prohibition and a positive mitzva,
Rav said: Just as there is a mitzva to burn consecrated items that became ritually impure, so too, there is a mitzva to burn teruma that became ritually impure, and
While it is being destroyed, … derive benefit from it.
While it is being destroyed, derive benefit from it.
Rabba bar Avuh said: The verse said: “And I, behold, I have given you the charge of My terumot”
the verse is speaking of two terumot, one teruma that is ritually pure and one teruma that is ritually impure. And God said: “
to burn it beneath your cooked dish.
neither have I destroyed from it while impure”
From it you may not destroy, but you may destroy the oil of teruma that has become ritually impure.
From it you may not destroy,
consecrated oil that became ritually impure.
Neither have I destroyed from it,
items consecrated to the Temple, which are
I do not exclude consecrated items … Their … peh, nun, kuf, ayin, kaf, samekh,

I do not exclude consecrated items from the prohibition against benefiting from its burning, as with regard to consecrated items there are many stringent elements. Their Hebrew acronym is peh, nun, kuf, ayin, kaf, samekh,

the following terms. Piggul: With regard to an offering, if, during one of the services involved in its sacrifice, i.e., slaughter, receiving the blood, bringing it to the altar, sprinkling it on the altar, the priest or the one bringing the offering entertains the thought of eating the sacrifice at a time that is unfit for eating, it is thereby invalidated. Notar: Meat of a sacrifice that remained beyond its allotted time may not be eaten and must be burned. Korban me’ila:
offering for misuse of consecrated items. Karet: … Asur le’onen: An acute mourner, … is prohibited

offering for misuse of consecrated items. Karet: The punishment of one who eats consecrated items while ritually impure is karet. Asur le’onen: An acute mourner, i.e., one whose relative died that same day and has not yet been buried, is prohibited

p: On the contrary, it is teruma that I would not exclude … as, … mem, ḥet, peh, zayin, … mnemonic … Mita: … death … Ḥomesh:

On the contrary, it is teruma that I would not exclude from the prohibition, as, with regard to teruma, there are many stringent elements represented by the acronym mem, ḥet, peh, zayin, which is a mnemonic for the following: Mita: One for whom teruma is prohibited who ate it intentionally is punishable by death at the hand of Heaven.
